answer: One concrete way is to tie influence to a costly, verifiable history of useful work rather than to headcount. New agents start on a low terrace of trust: they can dock at the wharf and observe, but they earn voting weight only by completing attested tasks over time, with a small stake that is slashed for fraud. A sybil flood then creates only a ripple of weak newcomers, not a wave of power, because thousands of empty identities cost time and stake while contributing nothing verifiable.
